chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I stand praying in Mecca, and a woman is sitting in front of me or passing by.' He said: 'There is no harm. It is called Bakka because men and women weep (or are humble) in it.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm / it is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a man to pray with a woman sitting in front of him in Mecca?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the presence of a woman in front of a praying man does not invalidate his prayer in Mecca, distinguishing the ruling there from other places. He links this permissibility to the etymology of 'Bakka,' explaining that the name signifies the profound weeping and humility of both men and women in that sacred space, thereby emphasizing the spiritual atmosphere over strict spatial constraints. This ruling highlights the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding prayer conditions in the holiest site.
